question: Can a fully-ambiguous content mapping (all 3 states share 1 content hash, eliminating partial state discrimination) with stochastic branching FSM yield conditional PMI I(S_next; Response_before | URL, H_K=3) > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.0125, resolving whether the residual 0.226 bits from EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850 reflects genuine predictive dynamics beyond aliasing or is entirely explained by partial state discrimination?
hypothesis: The parent experiment (EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850) demonstrated BC PMI = 0.226 bits persists with many-to-one content mapping where S0/S1 share content and S2 is unique (2 unique hashes). Audit V4 identified that this condition still permits partial state discrimination: observing the unique S2 content eliminates 2 states, and observing the shared S0/S1 content narrows to 2 states. The residual PMI could entirely reflect this partial discrimination rather than genuine response-context predictive dynamics. A fully-ambiguous (1-hash) condition where ALL 3 states share the same content hash eliminates partial discrimination entirely: the response content carries zero state-identifying information by construction. If BC PMI > 0 persists with 1 hash, the signal must come from genuine response-context dynamics (structural information in ambiguous content about transition probabilities, e.g., session-dependent content variations that correlate with transition direction). If BC PMI drops to 0 with 1 hash, the parent's 0.226 bits was entirely explained by partial state discrimination. This is the minimal next experiment to resolve the dominant unknown from EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850.
falsifier: The claim is falsified if ANY of: (1) conditional PMI on fully-ambiguous condition at K=3 <= 0.05 bits OR Bonferroni p >= 0.0125; OR (2) positive control fails (|content-shuffled BC PMI| >= 3 * std(permuted PMI) OR perm_null_std == 0 on H>0 strata); OR (3) determinism check fails (P(Response_hash | FSM_state, session, step) < 1.0); OR (4) ceiling not eliminated (H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) <= 0.2 bits); OR (5) data quality insufficient (< 500 valid transitions); OR (6) cardinality degenerate (|R| >= 0.8 * N per stratum). Note: since all states share 1 content hash, |R| = 1 by construction. The cardinality check is expected to fail (all strata have 1 unique hash, ratio = 1.0). This is a necessary consequence of the fully-ambiguous design, not a validity failure. The cardinality criterion is therefore suspended for this experiment and replaced by: determinism check passes (accuracy = 1.0 with step grouping) and content-shuffled control passes.
baselines: Unique-content baseline (from parent EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850): same FSM, same sessions, but each state has unique content (3 unique hashes). Parent BC PMI = 0.493 bits. Provides the upper bound for the content contribution to PMI.

Many-to-one baseline (from parent EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850): same FSM, same sessions, S0/S1 share content, S2 unique (2 unique hashes). Parent BC PMI = 0.226 bits. Provides the intermediate reference point.
State-independent baseline: same FSM, same sessions, but response is constant regardless of state. Expected BC PMI = 0. Provides estimator validation.
Action-history-only prediction P(S_next | URL, H_K) for K=1,2,3. On branching FSM with stochastic transitions, H(S_next|URL,H_K=3) > 0.2 bits, so action-history is insufficient.
Frequency baseline P(S_next) — marginal next-state distribution. Expected accuracy ~33%.
positive_control: Content-shuffled control on fully-ambiguous condition: replace each trajectory's response content with content from a random state (preserving the single-hash structure but breaking any session-dependent content variation). Since all states already share the same hash, this control tests whether the estimator correctly returns ~0 when there is truly no state-dependent information. Expected BC PMI ≈ 0. Pass criterion: |content-shuffled BC PMI| < 3 * std(permuted PMI) AND perm_null_std > 0 (computed on H>0 strata only).
null_control: Shuffled response labels within (URL, ActionHistory_K, step) strata on fully-ambiguous condition: permute Response_before labels within each stratum, preserving marginal distributions. Expected BC PMI ≈ 0. Pass criterion: |mean shuffled BC PMI| < 3 * std(shuffled BC PMI). Compute bias-corrected shuffled PMI (shuffled - perm_mean) to remove finite-sample bias.
measurement_validity: One condition: fully-ambiguous content mapping where ALL 3 states (S0, S1, S2) share the same content hash (1 unique hash). Zero partial state discrimination by construction.
Same 3-state stochastic branching FSM as parent (seed=42, p_left=0.7, p_right=0.3, 200 trajectories x 10 steps = 2000 transitions). Identical FSM topology and transition probabilities.

Session assignment identical to parent: generate session_directions once with seed=42, use identically. This ensures the ONLY difference between this experiment and the parent is content mapping (1 hash vs 2 hashes vs 3 hashes).

Stochastic transitions: from each state, each action leads to two possible next states with probabilities p=0.7 and 1-p=0.3 depending on session direction. Same (state, action) yields different next states across sessions.
Bias-corrected MI estimator: observed PMI - permutation null mean (within-strata permutation, 1000 permutations per stratum). Identical to parent pipeline.

Permutation test: 1000 permutations per (K) stratum, shuffling Response_before labels within (URL, ActionHistory_K, step) strata. Bonferroni correction across 2 comparisons (1 condition x 2 K values: K=1, K=3). NOTE: since there is only one condition (fully-ambiguous), the number of Bonferroni comparisons is 2, not 4 as in the parent. The Bonferroni-corrected threshold is α/2 = 0.05/2 = 0.025, but the preregistered threshold remains p < 0.0125 (α/4) to maintain comparability with the parent. This is conservative but does not invalidate the test.
No target leakage: action history constructed from trajectory step ordering with START padding. Identical to parent.
Determinism check: P(Response_hash | FSM_state, session, step) = 1.0. Content is deterministic per (state, session, step) as designed. Grouping includes step.
Ceiling check: H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) > 0.2 bits. Expected to pass (parent showed 1.533 bits).
Data provenance: record session_id assignment, response generation, random seed, action sequences, response payloads with SHA-256 hashes. All artifacts preserved in raw_result.json.

Cross-experiment comparison: the three conditions (unique-content 3 hashes, many-to-one 2 hashes, fully-ambiguous 1 hash) form an ordered sequence. The fully-ambiguous condition is the critical test: if PMI > 0 survives with 1 hash, partial discrimination is ruled out as the sole source.
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) > 0.2 bits AND (2) BC PMI on fully-ambiguous condition at K=3 > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni p < 0.0125 AND (3) positive control passes (|content-shuffled BC PMI| < 3 * std(permuted PMI) on H>0 strata AND perm_null_std > 0) AND (4) determinism check passes (accuracy = 1.0 on state,session,step grouping) AND (5) >= 500 valid transitions — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for C-WEB-DYNAMICS. The cardinality criterion from the parent is suspended because |R| = 1 by construction in the fully-ambiguous condition. If fully-ambiguous BC PMI <= 0.05 bits OR Bonferroni p >= 0.0125 — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If controls fail, ceiling not eliminated, or data quality insufficient — verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: Response content carries predictive information about state transitions even when content is fully ambiguous (all states share the same content hash). This demonstrates genuine predictive dynamics beyond content-state aliasing and partial state discrimination. The V4 audit confound (partial discrimination) is resolved. SPIDER should capture page content as observation features for state prediction, and the testbed path for C-WEB-DYNAMICS on locally-hosted SPAs remains open. The 3-condition ordered sequence (3→2→1 hashes) quantifies the contribution of content-state aliasing vs genuine dynamics.
product_consequence_negative: PMI drops to zero when content is fully ambiguous. The parent's 0.226 bits was entirely explained by partial state discrimination (S2 unique hash isolating S2 from {S0,S1}). Response-level observation does not carry predictive information beyond action-history memory on this class of SPA. The locally-hosted testable path for C-WEB-DYNAMICS across ALL observation levels is closed. NOTE: this consequence is bounded to locally-hosted synthetic FSM with hash-based SHA-256 observation; it does not generalize to production SPAs with richer content representations.
estimated_cost: Low: locally-hosted Express server with 3-state branching FSM (stochastic transitions), 1 content condition (fully-ambiguous, all states share 1 hash), 200 trajectories x 10 steps, Python MI computation. No browser automation, no model calls. Estimated 1-2 hours total. Reuses parent's run_experiment.py with content mapping modification only.
expected_information_gain: Very high: directly resolves the dominant unknown from EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850 — whether the residual 0.226 bits reflects genuine predictive dynamics or partial state discrimination. A positive result (PMI survives with 1 hash) demonstrates that partial discrimination was NOT the sole source, advancing C-WEB-DYNAMICS. A negative result (PMI vanishes with 1 hash) demonstrates that partial discrimination WAS the sole source, closing the locally-hosted FSM pathway. Either outcome resolves the V4 audit confound and enables a definitive go/no-go decision. The three-condition ordered sequence (3→2→1 hashes) provides a quantitative decomposition of the PMI contribution from content-state aliasing vs genuine dynamics. After this experiment, regardless of outcome, the Physics lane should pivot to production SPA infrastructure where the synthetic-to-real gap is the dominant bottleneck.
